```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = TRUE)
```

Work through this file alongside the chapter "Effects and Power" in the book. Keep it in the same folder as your `my_functions.R`.

## The data

```{r data}
scores <- c(44, 47, 48, 49, 50, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56)
```

## Load your toolbox

```{r load-toolbox}
library(tidyverse)
source("my_functions.R")
library(pwr)

all.equal(my_t_value(scores, 46), unname(t.test(scores, mu = 46)$statistic))
all.equal(my_p_value(my_t_value(scores, 46), df = 9), t.test(scores, mu = 46)$p.value)
all.equal(my_cutoffs(20:1, alpha = 0.1), c(2, 19))
```

You are looking for three `TRUE`s. If `library(pwr)` gives an error, install the package once with `install.packages("pwr")`.

## A world with an effect

Steves really are taller here: their heights have a mean of 180 cm, while everyone's have a mean of 175 cm. Both have an SD of 7 cm. Cohen's d is the difference in SDs:

```{r true-d}
(180 - 175) / 7
```

## Build both distributions

The second line is what `my_effect_t()` will do; you write it yourself further down.

```{r both-worlds}
null_ts <- replicate(1000, my_null_t(n = 10, pop_mean = 175, pop_sd = 7))
effect_ts <- replicate(
  1000, my_t_value(rnorm(n = 10, mean = 180, sd = 7), comparison_value = 175)
)

cutoffs <- my_cutoffs(null_ts)
cutoffs

hist(null_ts, breaks = 40, xlim = c(-5, 8), col = rgb(0.27, 0.48, 0.67, 0.5))
hist(effect_ts, breaks = 40, add = TRUE, col = rgb(0.84, 0.37, 0, 0.5))
abline(v = cutoffs, lty = 2)
```

## Counting

```{r count-both}
null_past <- null_ts < cutoffs[1] | null_ts > cutoffs[2]
effect_past <- effect_ts < cutoffs[1] | effect_ts > cutoffs[2]

tibble(
  world = c("null", "effect"),
  past = c(sum(null_past), sum(effect_past)),
  not_past = c(sum(!null_past), sum(!effect_past))
)
```

Which of these four numbers is the Type I error count? Which is the Type II error count? About how often did the groups of 10 Steves find the real 5 cm difference?

```{r my-effect-t}
my_effect_t(n = 10, pop_mean = 180, pop_sd = 7, comparison_value = 175)
```

### Check it against R

```{r my-effect-t-check}
set.seed(1)
mine <- my_effect_t(n = 10, pop_mean = 180, pop_sd = 7, comparison_value = 175)

set.seed(1)
r_version <- unname(
  t.test(rnorm(n = 10, mean = 180, sd = 7), mu = 175)$statistic
)

c(mine = mine, R = r_version)
all.equal(mine, r_version)
```

```{r my-power}
my_power <- function(ts, cutoffs) {
  past <-

}

my_power(effect_ts, cutoffs)
```

Power in a world with no effect:

```{r power-on-null}
my_power(null_ts, cutoffs)
```

### Check it: close enough

```{r power-check}
c(
  simulated = my_power(effect_ts, cutoffs),
  power.t.test = power.t.test(n = 10, delta = 5, sd = 7,
                              type = "one.sample")$power,
  pwr.t.test = pwr.t.test(n = 10, d = 5 / 7, type = "one.sample")$power
)

abs(
  my_power(effect_ts, cutoffs) -
    pwr.t.test(n = 10, d = 5 / 7, type = "one.sample")$power
) < 0.12
```

### Check it: d and t

The t-value is d multiplied by the square root of the sample size. Write that in code, then compare it with `my_t_value()`.

```{r my-cohens-d-check}
d_times_root_n <-
c(d_times_root_n = d_times_root_n, t = my_t_value(scores, 46))
all.equal(d_times_root_n, my_t_value(scores, 46))
```

## Add to your toolbox

1. Open `my_functions.R`.
2. Copy your finished `my_effect_t()`, `my_power()` and `my_cohens_d()` into it, under the **Effects and Power** heading. Copy only the functions.
3. Save `my_functions.R`.

Now check that the saved toolbox works on its own. You are looking for three `TRUE`s.

```{r toolbox-check}
rm(list = ls())
source("my_functions.R")

set.seed(1)
mine <- my_effect_t(n = 10, pop_mean = 180, pop_sd = 7, comparison_value = 175)
set.seed(1)
r_version <- unname(
  t.test(rnorm(n = 10, mean = 180, sd = 7), mu = 175)$statistic
)
all.equal(mine, r_version)

all.equal(my_power(c(-3, -1, 0, 1, 2.5), c(-2, 2)), 0.4)

scores <- c(44, 47, 48, 49, 50, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56)
all.equal(
  my_cohens_d(scores, 46) * sqrt(length(scores)),
  my_t_value(scores, 46)
)
```

If you see `could not find function`, that function is not in `my_functions.R` yet, or the file was not saved.
